For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/GLOBAL_ALLOCATOR_AND_MEGADRAW_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/GLOBAL_ALLOCATOR_AND_MEGADRAW_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
Traditional WebGL and naive WebGPU engines suffer from severe CPU-side overhead when rendering scenes with thousands of discrete mathematical objects:

items: **Buffer Thrashing**: Creating individual vertex (`VBO`) and index (`IBO`) buffers for each circle, line, arrow, or character incurs driver allocation costs and garbage collection overhead.
**BindGroup / State Churn**: Switching uniform bind groups and vertex buffer bindings per entity creates CPU submission stalls and pipeline validation bubbles.
**Draw Call Overhead**: Issuing thousands of `pass.drawIndexed()` calls per frame limits framerates on complex motion graphics compositions.

blocks.text: Retiam solves this through a unified **Global GPU Memory Pooling and Programmable Mega-Draw Batching** architecture:

items: **Single Global State Buffer**: All entity transforms, materials, and paint parameters reside in a single GPU storage buffer of 256-byte aligned slabs managed by [`GlobalStateAllocator.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/allocator/GlobalStateAllocator.ts).

**Single Global Geometry Buffer**: All 2D vector shapes, polygons, and triangulated paths sub-allocate ranges from massive shared vertex and index buffers managed by [`GlobalGeometryAllocator.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/allocator/GlobalGeometryAllocator.ts).

**Programmable Mega-Draw**: Batches thousands of distinct vector path draw packets into a **single WebGPU draw call** via storage buffer vertex-pulling in [`MegaDrawBatchManager.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/allocator/MegaDrawBatchManager.ts).

flowchart TD E["Scene entity tree"] --> S["GlobalStateAllocator
256-byte aligned slabs"] E --> G["GlobalGeometryAllocator

blocks.text: Every entity in Retiam maps its GPU state to a contiguous 256-byte slab (64 floats) inside a single global GPU Storage Buffer (`array<EntityState>`):

items: **Zero Memory Fragmentation**: Since all slabs are fixed at 256 bytes, slots can be recycled in $O(1)$ time without compaction.
**Single BindGroup**: `globalBindGroup` is bound once at Group 1 (`Pipeline.state_layout`). Shaders look up their state using the instance index without rebinding.

blocks.text: CPU writes to the local mirror `cpuData: Float32Array` are registered with [`DirtyBufferTracker.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/allocator/DirtyBufferTracker.ts):

items: Adjacent or closely-spaced dirty state slabs are automatically merged if the gap is smaller than a configurable margin threshold.
At the start of the frame, `allocator.flush()` transfers only modified slabs to GPU VRAM via minimal `device.queue.writeBuffer` calls.

blocks.text: All 2D vector shapes (`Path`, `Poly`, `Circle`, `Rect`, `Tex`, `SDFText`, `Axes`) sub-allocate from a pair of massive shared GPU buffers:

items: **`gpuVertexBuffer`**: Packed $(x, y)$ floats (8 bytes per vertex).
**`gpuIndexBuffer`**: Packed `Uint32` indices (4 bytes per index).
**Bump Allocation**: Initial allocations advance `_vertexHead` and `_indexHead`.
**Free Lists**: When an entity is destroyed or shrunk, its block is placed onto `_freeVertexBlocks` / `_freeIndexBlocks`. Subsequent allocations search for matching blocks before bumping.
**Dynamic Doubling**: When geometry exceeds capacity, the allocator creates a new buffer with double the size, copies existing data, updates GPU bind groups, and invalidates pipelines.

blocks.text: Instead of issuing hundreds of separate `pass.drawIndexed()` commands, `MegaDrawBatchManager` collapses multiple consecutive triangulated 2D path draw calls into a **single draw command**:
The GPU vertex shader fetches vertices and per-instance states entirely through storage buffers:

items: **Triangle Indexing**: The hardware vertex index `vi` determines the global triangle index:
**Draw Item Lookup**: The shader reads `triangleLookup[T]` to determine which `DrawItem` owns this triangle.
**Index Pulling**: It fetches the vertex index from `globalIndices[item.firstIndex + (T - item.firstTriangle) * 3 + corner] + item.firstVertex`.
**Vertex Pulling**: It loads the $(x, y)$ coordinate directly from `globalVertices`.
**State Unpacking**: It unpacks `item.packedInstance` to load world matrix, paint color, and opacity from `globalState`.

blocks.text: To convey both metadata flags and entity indices through standard WebGPU draw parameters without additional uniform buffers, Retiam uses a 32-bit packed instance format:

items: **Bit 31 (`S` - Stroke Flag)**: `1` if rendering a stroke, `0` if rendering a fill.
**Bit 30 (`M` - MegaDraw Flag)**: `1` if the draw call originates from `MegaDrawBatchManager`.
**Bits 29–16 (State Index)**: Identifies the 256-byte slab in `GlobalStateAllocator` (supports up to 16,384 active entities).
**Bits 15–0 (Local Start / Contour Index)**: Identifies the sub-contour or dash offset.
